div.head: Quadr Arg 28
div.ab: Et quæ per parentis riuulos probitatis fluuia passim diducta sunt, hic in unum bonitatis alueum redundare uideamus, ubi prolis inclitæ generosæ propagines umbram fessis potumque sitientibus grata perpetuitate conciliant.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 535 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Praise of William I, as above 16
nach Geburt mindestens zweier ehelicher Kinder Heinrichs, also nach 1103, geschrieben und bevor 1120 der Thronerbe Wilhelm ertrank. Vgl. u. S. 543i
written after the birth of at least two legitimate children of Henry, i.e. after 1103, and before the heir to the throne, William, was drowned in 1120. Cf. below p. 543i
so Hk [ob Emendation 16. Jhs.?]; per arentis, geänd. per arentes Dm; per arentes T
thus Hk [an emendation of the 16th cent.?]; per arentis, altered to per arentes Dm; per arentes T

div.ab: And the rivers of probity which have been drawn off here and there through the channels of his parent, let us see them here flow together into one bed of goodness, where the noble offshoots of the illustrious offspring provide, with pleasing perpetuity, shade for the weary and drink for the thirsty.
